issue: Does the bar in 28 U.S.C. § 2244(b)(1), which requires dismissal of a claim in a second or successive habeas application that was presented in a prior application, apply to second or successive motions by federal prisoners under § 2255?

sides.position: Section 2244(b)(1) applies to second or successive § 2255 motions, so a claim already presented in a prior motion must be dismissed.
cases: Gallagher v. United States, 711 F.3d 315 (2d Cir. 2013)
United States v. Winkelman, 746 F.3d 134 (3d Cir. 2014)
Winarske v. United States, 913 F.3d 765 (8th Cir. 2019)

sides.position: Section 2244(b)(1) does not apply to second or successive § 2255 motions; such claims are instead analyzed under the gateway provisions of § 2255(h).
cases: Jones v. United States, 36 F.4th 974 (9th Cir. 2022)

this_court: Section 2244(b)(1) does not apply to second or successive § 2255 motions; such claims are analyzed under § 2255(h).
quote: Our sister circuits are divided on the matter whether the bar in § 2244(b)(1) applies to second or successive § 2255 motions, and our court has not yet decided that question.
cite: Willie Jones, Sr. v. United States, 36 F.4th 974 (9th Cir. 2022)
